quiz_metadata.title: Model Evaluation, ROC, Lift & Profit Curves
quiz_metadata.description: Comprehensive graduate-level practice quiz evaluating model metrics, threshold optimization, lift curves, ROC analysis, and profit/business decision-making.
quiz_metadata.author: BU-Stats-Questionaire

questions.section: Section 1: Classification Fundamentals & Confusion Matrix Relationships
questions.question_text: Given a confusion matrix with 80 True Positives (TP), 20 False Negatives (FN), 30 False Positives (FP), and 870 True Negatives (TN), the True Positive Rate (TPR / Sensitivity) is ____ and the False Positive Rate (FPR) is ____.
questions.learning_objective: Understanding of AUC, thresholds, confusion matrix relationships

questions.section: Section 1: Classification Fundamentals & Confusion Matrix Relationships
questions.question_text: In a dataset with 50 positive instances and 950 negative instances, a naive model that predicts every observation as negative achieves an accuracy of ____ %, a recall of ____ %, and a precision of ____.
questions.explanation: Accuracy = (0 + 950) / 1000 = 95%. Recall = 0 / (0 + 50) = 0%. Precision = TP / (TP + FP) = 0 / 0, which is mathematically undefined.
questions.learning_objective: Understanding of AUC, thresholds, confusion matrix relationships

questions.section: Section 1: Classification Fundamentals & Confusion Matrix Relationships
questions.question_text: The fundamental mathematical distinction between ranking and classification is that classification outputs a discrete ____, whereas ranking produces a continuous ____ or probability score that sorts observations.
questions.explanation: Classification assigns a hard categorical class label (e.g., 0 or 1) based on a decision threshold, while ranking assigns continuous scores/probabilities to order instances relative to each other.

questions.section: Section 1: Classification Fundamentals & Confusion Matrix Relationships
questions.question_text: To convert a ranking model's predicted probability into a binary classifier decision, an analyst must select a specific decision ____.
questions.explanation: A decision threshold (e.g., 0.50 or 0.20) cuts continuous ranked scores into discrete binary class predictions (1 if score >= threshold, else 0).
questions.learning_objective: Understanding of AUC, thresholds, confusion matrix relationships

questions.question_text: The Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve plots the metric ____ on the y-axis against the metric ____ on the x-axis across all possible decision thresholds.
questions.correct_answer: True Positive Rate (TPR / Sensitivity), False Positive Rate (FPR / 1-Specificity)
questions.explanation: An ROC curve evaluates classifier performance across thresholds by placing TPR on the y-axis and FPR on the x-axis.

questions.question_text: An Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) value of ____ indicates a completely random classifier, while an AUC of ____ indicates a perfect classifier.
questions.explanation: AUC = 0.50 represents baseline performance equivalent to random guessing (diagonal line), while AUC = 1.00 represents perfect separation with zero false positives or false negatives.
questions.learning_objective: Understanding of AUC, thresholds, confusion matrix relationships

questions.question_text: If a targeted marketing campaign contacts the top 10% scored population and achieves a 25% response rate, compared to a overall base population response rate of 5%, the calculated Lift score for the top decile is ____.
questions.explanation: Lift = (Model Target Response Rate) / (Base Response Rate) = 25% / 5% = 5.0.

questions.question_text: On a standard cumulative response (lift) chart, a Lift factor of ____ indicates that the model performs no better than selecting targets completely at random.
questions.explanation: A lift of 1.0 means the model's response rate in the selected sample equals the random population base rate.

questions.question_text: In a credit card fraud detection model, lowering the classification threshold from 0.50 to 0.10 will cause Sensitivity (Recall) to ____ and Specificity to ____.
questions.explanation: Lowering the decision threshold classifies more instances as positive, capturing more true fraud (increasing Sensitivity) but incorrectly flagging more legitimate transactions as fraud (decreasing Specificity).
questions.learning_objective: Understanding of AUC, thresholds, confusion matrix relationships

questions.question_text: The slope of an ROC curve at any given point $(FPR, TPR)$ is mathematically equal to the ratio of ____ to ____ required to justify moving the decision threshold to that point under cost-benefit conditions.
questions.correct_answer: marginal net cost of False Positives, marginal net benefit of True Positives
questions.explanation: The optimal operating point on an ROC curve occurs where the slope $d(TPR)/d(FPR) = [P(N)/P(P)] \cdot [(C_{FP} - C_{TN}) / (B_{TP} - C_{FN})]$. The slope equals the cost ratio scaled by class priors.

questions.question_text: When calculating expected profit for a marketing campaign, if $N = 10,000$, TP = 400, FP = 1,600, profit per true positive $B_{TP} = \$50$, and cost per targeting action $C_{FP} = \$5$, the total net profit generated is $\$____.

A customer churn detection model generates an AUC of 0.88, but when deployed at a standard probability threshold of 0.50, it yields zero flagged customers. Which of the following best explains this behavior?
options: A) The model has severe over-fitting and must be regularized using Ridge regression.
B) The background churn rate (base rate) is extremely low, causing all predicted probabilities to fall below 0.50 despite excellent ranking order.
C) The ROC curve is non-convex, rendering AUC mathematically invalid.
D) The model suffers from high multicollinearity between predictor variables.
questions.explanation: AUC measures ranking ability independent of thresholds. In heavily imbalanced datasets (e.g., 1% churn), maximum predicted probabilities may only reach 0.25. While ranking is strong (AUC 0.88), a default 0.50 threshold yields zero positive predictions, requiring threshold tuning.

questions.question_text: An executive team asks why Model A is preferred over Model B for direct mailing targeting when Model B has a higher overall accuracy (92% vs 85%). What is the primary conceptual flaw in relying on accuracy for this decision?
options: A) Accuracy ignores the total size of the test dataset.

B) Accuracy assumes equal misclassification costs and static class proportions, ignoring that false negatives (missing a customer) and false positives (mailing cost) have radically different financial consequences.
C) Accuracy cannot be calculated from a confusion matrix without knowing the AUC.
D) Accuracy fluctuates whenever non-linear decision trees are utilized instead of logistic regression.
questions.explanation: Accuracy implicitly assumes symmetric error costs ($C_{FP} = C_{FN}$) and uniform class distribution. In targeted mailing, costs are asymmetric ($C_{FP} = \text{cost of stamp}$, $C_{FN} = \text{lost sale}$), making profit curves or lift metrics far superior to accuracy.

questions.question_text: When comparing an ROC curve to a cumulative Lift curve for a loan default prediction system, which statement correctly describes their structural difference?
options: A) The ROC curve depends on net monetary profit, whereas the Lift curve depends strictly on log-loss.
B) The ROC curve compares TPR against FPR independent of class priors, whereas the Lift curve evaluates cumulative positive capture relative to targeted population percentage.
C) The Lift curve requires a fixed 0.50 decision threshold, whereas the ROC curve varies the threshold from 0 to 1.
D) An ROC curve can never cross the diagonal line, whereas a Lift curve always crosses zero.
questions.explanation: ROC curves plot TPR vs. FPR across thresholds without embedding class proportions on the x-axis. Lift curves explicitly plot response gain/lift as a function of the cumulative percentage of the population targeted, making lift directly tied to campaign size.

questions.question_text: A health insurance firm is building a Capstone project model to predict rare high-cost hospital readmissions (1% of cases). The data science lead mandates using Precision-Recall (PR) curves instead of ROC curves. Why?
options: A) ROC curves are computationally inefficient for sample sizes under 100,000.
B) Precision-Recall curves do not require calculating False Positives.
C) In heavily imbalanced datasets, large True Negative counts dilute the FPR in ROC curves, presenting an overly optimistic view of model performance.
D) PR curves always have an area under the curve equal to 1.0.
questions.explanation: Because TN is extremely large in highly imbalanced data, $FPR = FP / (FP + TN)$ remains tiny even when FP is large. This makes ROC curves look deceptive, whereas Precision ($TP / (TP + FP)$) directly reflects false positive contamination.

questions.question_text: You evaluate a marketing response model on 10,000 customers with a 5% baseline response rate. If you target the top 20% of scored customers and obtain a Lift of 3.0, how many responders (True Positives) did you successfully capture?
questions.explanation: Targeted population = 20% of 10,000 = 2,000 customers. Baseline response rate = 5%. Model response rate = Lift * Baseline = 3.0 * 5% = 15%. Responders captured = 15% of 2,000 = 300 True Positives.

questions.question_text: An analyst plots a profit curve for a subscription renewal campaign where contacting a customer costs $10 and a successful renewal yields $100 net benefit. The profit curve reaches its absolute maximum at a population target percentile of 15%. What does this peak represent?
options: A) The point where model accuracy reaches 100%.
B) The operational cutoff where marginal revenue of contacting the next ranked customer equals the marginal cost ($10).
C) The threshold where True Positives equal False Positives.
D) The location where the ROC curve has an slope of exactly 1.0.
questions.explanation: Profit curves plot cumulative net profit against targeted percentage. The maximum profit peak occurs precisely where marginal return equals marginal cost; beyond 15%, the expected probability of renewal is too low to cover the $10 contact cost.

questions.question_text: In a capstone research proposal for financial fraud detection, why is it critical to define misclassification costs prior to selecting a final deployment model?
options: A) Because cost matrices are required to prove that model feature residuals are normally distributed.
B) Because the optimal model selection and decision threshold depend directly on the relative ratio of fraud loss vs user friction cost.
C) Because models trained without cost metrics cannot calculate AUC.
D) Because unsupervised learning algorithms require cost parameters to converge.
questions.explanation: A model selected purely on AUC or accuracy may perform poorly in production if the actual business cost of missing a fraud ($1,000) far outweighs the friction cost of a false alert ($5). The cost structure dictates threshold choice and model ranking.

questions.question_text: Suppose Model Alpha and Model Beta both have an AUC of 0.85. However, Model Alpha's ROC curve dominates Model Beta's in the FPR range of [0.0, 0.10], while Model Beta dominates in the FPR range of [0.30, 0.80]. If operating in a high-security setting where FPR must be kept under 5%, which model should be selected?
options: A) Model Beta, because it maintains superior performance over a wider total range of FPR values.
B) Model Alpha, because its ROC curve is superior in the specific low-FPR region enforced by business constraints.
C) Either model, because identical AUC values guarantee equal profitability.
D) Neither model; a linear regression must be used instead.
questions.explanation: Global AUC aggregates performance over all operating points (0 to 1). When operating under strict business constraints (FPR < 5%), regional ROC dominance dictates selection. Model Alpha is superior in the specific operating window.

questions.question_text: When interpreting a Lift curve, what does a horizontal Lift line at a value of 1.0 across all population deciles signify?
options: A) Perfect model sorting with zero false positives.
B) A model whose predictions are completely uninformative and equivalent to random targeting.
C) A model applied to a dataset with a 100% positive base rate.
D) An over-fitted model that requires cross-validation.
questions.explanation: Lift = (Model Response Rate / Base Rate). A constant lift of 1.0 means every decile returns the exact same proportion of positives as a random sample, indicating zero predictive power.

questions.section: Section 5: Advanced Strategy, Profit Modeling & Storytelling
questions.question_text: A retail bank is evaluating two churn models for high-value wealth accounts ($100,000 average balance). Model 1 has AUC = 0.90 but its highest lift is concentrated in the top 30% of risk scores. Model 2 has AUC = 0.82 but achieves a Lift of 6.0 in the top 5% of risk scores. The retention team has budget to contact only 5% of accounts. Which model maximizes business profit and why?
options: A) Model 1, because its higher overall AUC guarantees greater overall financial returns across the entire portfolio.
B) Model 2, because under a strict 5% capacity constraint, its superior local lift in the top ventile captures significantly more at-risk revenue than Model 1.
C) Model 1, because high AUC models automatically eliminate False Positive contact costs.
D) Model 2, but only if the decision threshold is set to 0.50 regardless of population distribution.
questions.explanation: Business capacity constraints dictate the operational window. Since only 5% can be targeted, Model 2's local Lift of 6.0 in the top 5% captures far more churners than Model 1, making Model 2 more profitable despite having a lower global AUC.

questions.section: Section 5: Advanced Strategy, Profit Modeling & Storytelling
questions.question_text: An e-commerce firm uses a model to offer a $20 discount code to prevent cart abandonment. Margin per sale is $100 (without discount). Issuing a discount to a customer who would have bought anyway yields $80 margin (FP cost = $20 lost margin). Failing to target an abandoner yields $0 (FN). Targeting an abandoner who then buys yields $80 profit ($100 - $20). If the base abandonment rate is 20%, what is the optimal decision threshold rule in terms of predicted abandonment probability $P(Abandon)$?
options: A) Target if $P(Abandon) > 0.50$
B) Target if $P(Abandon) > 0.20$
C) Target if $P(Abandon) > 0.25$
D) Target if $P(Abandon) > 0.80$
questions.explanation: Expected profit of targeting = $P(Abandon) \cdot 80 + (1 - P(Abandon)) \cdot 80 = 80$. Expected profit of NOT targeting = $P(Abandon) \cdot 0 + (1 - P(Abandon)) \cdot 100 = 100(1 - P(Abandon))$. Equating both: $80 = 100 - 100 P(Abandon) \implies 100 P(Abandon) = 20 \implies P(Abandon) = 0.20$ threshold mathematically? Re-evaluating net benefit: Benefit of targeting true abandoner = $80. Cost of targeting non-abandoner = $20 lost margin. Threshold $p^* = \frac{\text{Cost}}{\text{Benefit}} = \frac{20}{80} = 0.25$. Target when $P(Abandon) > 0.25$.

questions.section: Section 5: Advanced Strategy, Profit Modeling & Storytelling
questions.question_text: You are presenting a customer churn prevention proposal to the CMO. Model performance shows high ROC-AUC (0.86), but the CMO is skeptical of abstract metrics. Which executive visual communication package best follows actionable storytelling design guidelines to drive strategic investment?
options: A) Present a single slide containing the raw ROC curve, define AUC in a bullet list, and recommend that leadership adopt machine learning to improve retention context.

B) Display a profit curve chart highlighting the maximum profit point at 12% target population; color the peak point bright green while keeping baseline costs gray; add a callout annotation showing '+$1.2M Net Revenue at 12% targeting'; and end with the recommended action: 'Allocate $150k campaign budget to target top 12% scored churn risks.'
C) Present a table listing accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, and F1-score across ten candidate models, and request the CMO choose the preferred threshold.
D) Show a generic bar chart of model accuracy with high-contrast colors, gridlines, and a subtitle stating 'Machine Learning Drives Action'.
questions.explanation: Meets all executive storytelling requirements: uses a specific concrete visual (profit curve), applies explicit visual hierarchy (bright green peak, gray baseline), includes a concrete annotation (+$1.2M Net Revenue), and specifies a concrete business action (allocate $150k to target top 12%).

questions.section: Section 5: Advanced Strategy, Profit Modeling & Storytelling
questions.question_text: A fintech enterprise detects fraudulent transactions. System A utilizes a Random Forest (AUC = 0.93). System B utilizes Logistic Regression (AUC = 0.87). However, System A requires 400 milliseconds latency per transaction (causing user cart drop-off costing $500,000/year), whereas System B operates in 10 milliseconds. Profit curve analysis accounting for latency friction shows System B yields $3.2M net annual benefit versus System A's $2.7M. What is the correct capstone recommendation?
options: A) Deploy System A because AUC is the sole definitive statistical metric for model quality.
B) Deploy System B because incorporating operational friction costs into the financial evaluation proves it achieves higher net profitability despite lower AUC.
C) Reject both systems and retrain using unsupervised clustering until AUC exceeds 0.99.
D) Deploy System A and disable latency logging to remove friction metrics from evaluation.
questions.explanation: Real-world model deployment requires evaluating total operational profitability. When transaction latency costs ($500k) are factored into the profit framework, System B generates higher net business value ($3.2M vs $2.7M), making it the superior deployment choice.

questions.section: Section 5: Advanced Strategy, Profit Modeling & Storytelling
questions.question_text: You are designing a dashboard slide to persuade an executive committee to adjust the credit card fraud alert threshold. Which specific set of design choices complies with concrete design rules for actionable storytelling?
options: A) Use a visual framework to explain context, optimize decluttering, focus visual attention, and encourage strategic action.

B) Display a slopegraph comparing current $0.50 threshold vs proposed $0.15 threshold fraud loss; highlight savings in dark green and false-alert costs in light gray; add a callout annotation showing '+$450k net loss reduction'; and include a call-to-action: 'Lower alert threshold to $0.15 on October 1.'
C) Create a 3D pie chart showing confusion matrix ratios with default software color palettes and gridlines to show data completeness.
D) Provide a high-level overview chart with abstract labels like 'Visual Focus' and 'Dashboard Alignment' without displaying dollar values.
questions.explanation: Option B contains at least 3 concrete design actions (slopegraph choice, dark green/light gray visual emphasis, +$450k annotation) and provides a concrete business decision ('Lower alert threshold to $0.15 on October 1'). Option A uses prohibited abstract placeholders.

questions.section: Section 5: Advanced Strategy, Profit Modeling & Storytelling
questions.question_text: A subscription news platform experiences 5% monthly user churn. A machine learning model ranks users by churn risk. The marketing team can offer a $5/month price discount for 6 months ($30 total cost) or an email re-engagement campaign ($0.50 cost, 10% success rate). Profit curve modeling reveals that applying the price discount to the top 3% and the email campaign to deciles 4-10 maximizes LTV. Which strategic action should leadership take?
options: A) Offer the $30 price discount to 100% of subscribers to maximize total retention volume.

B) Apply a multi-tier intervention: route top 3% highest-risk users to the $30 discount incentive, route deciles 4-10 to the $0.50 email campaign, and leave low-risk users uncontacted to prevent margin erosion.
C) Eliminate all retention marketing because email campaigns have a low (10%) success rate.
D) Select a single threshold at 0.50 probability and offer the discount to everyone above that threshold.
questions.explanation: Maximizing profit curves across tiered interventions requires matching cost/benefit profiles to risk deciles. High-cost, high-impact interventions ($30 discount) are profitable only for extreme-risk users (top 3%), while low-cost interventions ($0.50 email) are suitable for moderate risk, optimizing overall LTV.
